clue.text: Skirt lassie originally packed in clothes

indicators.note: packed in says the lassie's letter is stuffed inside the word for clothes

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes, as in football kit

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word lassie

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl's first step: her skirt goes into the luggage with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives L, the first letter of 'lassie', and 'packed in' puts it inside KIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland garment worn by Scots is a pleated tartan skirt.

clue.text: Recoil, seeing daughter with unusual percussion instrument

parts.note: a gun's kick is its recoil
rum means odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A girl flinches on hearing an odd bit of the drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass drum in a kit, struck by a pedal, is a drum for rhythm.

clue.text: Old railway company engages old recluse

indicators.note: engages means takes on or holds, so the company holds the letter inside

parts.note: the LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway, a pre-1948 British company

explanation.surface: A defunct railway firm hires an elderly hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives alone, avoiding company: a solitary person.

clue.text: Supports No. 1 baseball player

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the top is number one, the best

explanation.surface: A clue praising the star of a ball team who props everyone up.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball the catcher behind home plate is called the backstop.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstop is American slang for the catcher, the player crouched behind the batter.

clue.text: Made burglar-proof? Not quite completely protected

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: all means wholly or completely
armed means equipped with weapons, protected

explanation.surface: A house fitted with security is not entirely safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts ALL to AL. The question mark marks the definition as a description rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A house fitted with a burglar alarm is protected against break-ins.

clue.text: Gentleman left in the bar, choking badly

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for left goes inside the rearranged letters
badly says the words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man left at the pub chokes horribly on his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges THEBARCHOKING, and 'in' sets L among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Knight Bachelor is a man knighted without membership of an order, so titled Sir.

clue.text: Taste before swallowing one new type of citrus fruit

parts.note: tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: swallowing says the word for before takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Sample a novel fruit by eating one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts I and N inside ERE to make ERINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned orange from Tangier, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: Stake a large amount

definitions.meaning: a post driven into the ground to support a building
a heap or great quantity, as of money

explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a post sunk as a foundation, and also a heap of something.

clue.text: Investors have no preference for such stock

definitions.text: Investors have no preference for such stock

parts.words: Investors have no preference for such stock
parts.note: preference shares rank above the common kind, so stock with no preference is the plain everyday type

explanation.surface: Shareholders are indifferent about some holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no preference' reads as indifference, but preference shares are a class of stock; the answer is the class without preference.
explanation.definitionFit: Common equity in a company, ranking after preference stock for dividends.

clue.text: Burning tree is seen in one

indicators.note: is seen in says the tree appears inside the word one

parts.note: taken as written
a fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: A conifer catches light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alight is ablaze, with flames.

clue.text: Dicky, collared by fellow-citizen, keen to fight

indicators.note: collared by says the dicky is held inside, as a neck is held by a collar

parts.note: a conational is someone of the same nation
a dicky is a false shirt front

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell is grabbed by the collar by a compatriot spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like 'unwell', but it is the detachable shirt front, FRONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confrontational is aggressive and eager for argument or combat.

clue.text: This theory ingeniously draws in origins of inherent multiplicity

indicators.note: ingeniously says the letters are cleverly rearranged
origins of points to the opening letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A theory that cleverly pulls in the sources of inherited variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' gives I and M; 'ingeniously' rearranges DRAWSIN with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution by natural selection is the theory named after its Victorian proposer.

clue.text: Hastened to take cover, say

indicators.note: say indicates the word is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to hide is to take cover

explanation.surface: Someone ran off quickly to get under shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an old verb for hurry, so its past tense means hurried.

clue.text: One expelled from Italian region, say, over offence

indicators.note: expelled from says the single letter is thrown out of the region's name

parts.note: Umbria is a region of central Italy
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: over says the abbreviation is read backwards in a down light

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Someone banished from part of Italy takes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled from' drops I from UMBRIA to leave UMBRA; 'over' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so the noun means resentment.

clue.text: Madame Bovary's Mr Right?

parts.note: a Frenchwoman like Flaubert's heroine would call her perfect man a French phrase meaning ideal sweetheart

explanation.surface: Flaubert's heroine dreams of the perfect man.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma Bovary is French, so her Mr Right is a French-flavoured phrase, literally a perfect lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a perfect type of excellence, and literally an ideal suitor.

clue.text: Workin' on foreign language version of film Grease

indicators.note: the apostrophe in workin' shows a final G dropped, so the same is done to the next word

parts.note: dubbing replaces a film's dialogue with another language

explanation.surface: A projectionist busy on a translated film gets oil on their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workin'' drops its G, and so does DUBBING, leaving the waterproofing grease used on leather boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbin is a waxy grease rubbed into leather to soften and waterproof it.

clue.text: Conference provider

parts.note: Conference is a variety of pear, so what yields it is the plant bearing that fruit

explanation.surface: A firm that hosts business meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conference' suggests a meeting; it is a popular British pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Conference pears grow on that fruit-bearing plant.

clue.text: Woodland creatures of old remained years afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards says the years come after the word for remained

parts.note: sat means stayed or remained

explanation.surface: Mythical forest beings stayed put for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these goat-legged spirits of the woods followed Dionysus.

clue.text: Get tougher US politician to put over argument

indicators.note: to put over means placed round, so the politician wraps the argument

parts.note: Sen is the abbreviation for a US senator
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: An American senator gets firm in pressing his case.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen is to become harder or more rigid.

clue.text: Ally cut by revolutionary weapon

indicators.note: cut by says the friend is split open by the revolutionary

parts.note: a mate is a friend or ally
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A friend is slashed by a rebel's blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy knife used as a tool and a weapon in Latin America.

clue.text: Power, namely, in grasp of drug courier

indicators.note: in grasp of says the abbreviation is held inside the courier

parts.note: a mule smuggles drugs for others
sc is short for scilicet, Latin for namely

explanation.surface: Namely, the force a drug smuggler has in his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means strength or force, as in financial clout.

clue.text: Bah! Drink is rejected by husband

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the drink is read backwards

parts.note: to sip is to drink

explanation.surface: A wife scoffs as her husband turns down a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pish is an exclamation of contempt or impatience, like pooh.

clue.text: One scrutinising popular magazine thanklessly

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: thanklessly means without ta, the British word for thanks

parts.note: The Spectator is a British weekly magazine

explanation.surface: Someone reading a well-liked periodical gets no gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for 'thank you', so 'thanklessly' takes it out of SPECTATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector examines things closely, checking them officially.

clue.text: After childish game, one's mostly cross

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the game

parts.note: tig is a children's chasing game, also called tag

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: After a playground game, a child is feeling grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ONE to ON. 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is a noun: a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: The tigon is a hybrid bred from a male tiger and a lioness.

clue.text: Pack some clothes to wear

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Put some outfits in the suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to put away or load things into a space.

clue.text: Petty criminal, dolt father urged to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stupid man's dad pushes him to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the young pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's pickpocket from Oliver Twist is a small-time thief.

clue.text: Town acclaimed by Berliners in 1989?

parts.note: in 1989 Berliners cheered the fall of their dividing barrier, so a town name split in two describes what they celebrated

explanation.surface: Germans in 1989 cheered a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyneside town, read as two words, is what Berliners cheered when their Wall came down.
explanation.definitionFit: A town near Newcastle on the Tyne, at the eastern end of Hadrian's barrier.

clue.text: Channel Four girl

indicators.note: four tells you to take a run of four letters from inside the word channel

explanation.surface: A woman working on a British television network.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel Four is a UK TV station; here 'Four' says take four letters from inside 'Channel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, as for the Princess Royal.
